title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and purpose. These notes study the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. The boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification is a normal-crossings divisor. D_d is the (normalised) multiplicity of curves with d marked nodes (a chosen set of d nodes), with open part D*_d, so the closed stratum of codimension d is the image of D_d. A strict flag d_* = {d_0 > d_1 > ... > d_r} labels a 'simplex' of the stratification. D_{d_0,...,d_r} parametrises curves with d_0 nodes plus nested chosen subsets of nodes of sizes d_1 ⊃ ... ⊃ d_r. P*_{d_*} is a deleted tubular neighbourhood (the 'link' at infinity along the flag). Grothendieck wants a functor from the category of such simplices to fundamental groupoids. To each simplicial map α: Δ_r → Δ_{r'} he attaches a map of groupoids Π_{Δ_{r'}} → Π_{Δ_r} of type 'specialisation' (eq. 219, previous page).

The page's argument.
1. α factors as a surjection (degeneracy) followed by an injection (face).
2. In the degenerate case, (219) is an isomorphism, or at least a smooth, finite-type, essentially trivial map. A repeated index just repeats the same stratum.
3. So one is reduced to injective 'specialisations' (faces). The only problematic case is α(0) ≠ 0, i.e. the deepest stratum d_0 is dropped: d'_* ⊂ d_*, d'_0 < d_0.
4. One then needs the homomorphism (222) π_1 P*_{d_0,...,d_r} → π_1 P*_{d'_0,...,d'_r}.
5. To build it he notes the forgetful map (223) D_{d_0,...,d_r} → D_{d'_0,...,d'_r}. This keeps the curve but remembers only the chosen subsets. It is a map between the closed (non-*) multiplicities only: it does not send D* into D*. It is a local immersion of smooth algebraic multiplicities of codimension d_0 − d'_0, which is correct for a normal-crossings boundary (smoothing d_0 − d'_0 nodes).
6. The margin reduces to strictly decreasing d_i and singles out D_{d_0,d_1,...,d_r} → D_{d_1,...,d_r} for α(0) ≠ 0.
7. The next page completes this with a square: D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*} over D_{d_0,d'_0} → D*_{d'_0}, with étale verticals, cartesian when d'_0 = d_1. It then pulls back the boundary divisors Θ and their p-skeleta to analyse the deleted neighbourhoods.

In modern terms: this builds the 'exit-path'/stratified fundamental groupoid of the normal-crossings stack M̄_{g,ν} along chains of strata. The π_1 of each link is an extension of the stratum's π_1 by the free abelian group of Dehn twists around the nodes. Specialisation maps between links of nested strata are obtained from the local-immersion structure of normalised strata.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claimed codimension d_0 − d'_0 and the remark that (223) exists only on closed, non-starred strata are correct for normal-crossings boundaries.
Gap: the homomorphism (222) is only announced here; its construction (via the tubular structure and the cartesian square) is deferred to the next page.

ideas.what: Functor from the category of strict flags of boundary strata (simplices) to fundamental groupoids of deleted tubular neighbourhoods; reduction to degeneracies and faces
ideas.modern_name: exit-path / stratified fundamental groupoid of a normal-crossings stratification (also: Kato–Nakayama log Betti space restricted to strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths), Treumann 2009, Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix A); for the log side Kato–Nakayama 1999
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches 'structure à l'infini', tubular neighbourhoods and tame topology, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Forgetful map of normalised strata D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*} as a local immersion of codimension d_0 − d'_0, defined only on closed strata
ideas.modern_name: normalisation of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}; stable-graph contraction maps

ideas.what: Specialisation homomorphisms between π_1 of links of nested strata (Dehn-twist extensions)
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points / specialisation maps at infinity of M_{g,n}; Teichmüller groupoid at infinity
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, in spirit)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, for the DM boundary, a simplicially indexed system of fundamental groupoids of deleted tubular neighbourhoods along flags of strata, with face/degeneracy functoriality. This anticipates exit-path categories and log (Kato–Nakayama) homotopy types of M̄_{g,ν}, which were developed later and independently.
missed.quote: il faut considérer l'homomorphisme (222) π_1 P*_{d_0,...,d_r} → π_1 P*_{d'_0,...,d'_r}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precedence for stratified/exit-path homotopy applied to moduli at infinity. It also points to a systematic algebraic (profinite) version via log étale fundamental groups of the boundary strata.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in a larger unpublished construction of a stratified fundamental-groupoid formalism at infinity of M_{g,ν}. The ideas are now standard (exit paths, Dehn-twist extensions), but the early systematic simplicial formulation is notable. The page itself has only routine geometric facts.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: it should read 'spécialisation injective' (underlined), not 'non-injective'. The previous page reduces to the surjective/degenerate and the injective cases, the surjective one is disposed of, so the injective (face) case remains. Very likely '(à l'opposition « face »)'.
Under (223): read '(mais non un morphisme entre les espaces * !)': the map exists between closed strata but not between the open starred ones.
Read 'qui est une immersion (locale) de multiplicités algébriques lisses, de codimension d_0 − d'_0'. This is consistent with the next page's 'immersion locale de codimension d = d_0 − d'_0'.
In (222) the first subscript was corrected: d_0, (crossed) d_1, ..., d_r.
